title: Jerome Carrington and the Mosley brothers in Chicago
summary: Palmer recalls musicians he met on arriving in Chicago, Jerome Carrington and the Francois Mosley band at the Golden Lily.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you play much in Chicago in the late 20s? No. I didn't do much playing here. I came came here at the hospital. But I think you know Jerome Carrington? He was the first musician I met.

He's one of the first musicians I met in Chicago. In Chicago? Yeah, very nice looking boy. He's dead now. Yes, he died in... no, I don't know. He played... He's dead. Yeah. I met his nephew here the other night. Really? Yeah, his nephew played. What's his name? Oh, Carrington. I don't know his first name, but I knew he was Carrington. That's his nephew. Yeah, yeah. Could you tell me more about Jerome Carrington?
Where did you meet him in Chicago? Where did he play? In a band or solo? Yeah, he was playing at the...
Oh, when I first came here, he was playing at the Nest when I came here. The Nest? Down on 135th Street. I mean down 35th Street, you know, 100th Street, that's New York. But yeah,
I met him here. He was... I know he was playing in a band called Frankie Franco and his Louisiana. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. From French Miller. They played at the Golden Lily. Yeah. That's right.

You know French? Uh, I want to meet him in New Orleans. Yeah, he's... Did you go to meet him? Yeah. I want to go to New Orleans. Oh, he knows... French knows me well. He knows you well? Oh, sure. French knows me well. Did you play together? No, I never did play with him, but he, uh, he knows my wife. He works for my wife. He, uh, French used to be with the Francois band. French, Francois Mosley, the drummer. Yeah, Francois Mosley. Yeah. Yeah. This band played at the Golden Lily. Yeah, yeah, yeah. He used to be with that band. Did you see that band? Yeah. The Golden Lily? Yeah. Yeah. Did you, Craig? No, before they went there. I'd probably had to see it. Yeah, Francois liked to wake up to have a good band. I had a piano player named Todd. I forget about those boys. Yeah, there's no point in just going along with what they're playing in these days. They had quite a... Oh, I can't think. No, I can't. I just can't think of things like I use, you know. My mind isn't that good, you know, for my condition. I can't think. I can tell you some of them in the band, but I can't. No, I can't think of them. I know, uh, Francois, I know him. He's got his brothers. In fact, all them boys played. He's got a whole bunch of them. Whose brother? All of them. The brothers. The Mosley brothers. Mosley. Yeah.
Did they play in the North? Or... He was from New Orleans, you know?
Yeah, but they all did the most of the playing here.
Yes. And his brothers? Yeah. Also played around here?
They had a big band together. Here in Chicago? Yeah. They... quite a bunch of musicians.
